title: Recursive Continuation Semantics

basis.scope: Introduce recursive continuation structure as the first expressiveness extension after bounded strategy correctness; explicit recursion is guarded and depth-bounded, bounded unfolding may defer as pNF(C), and recovery, sigma_RT, and operational-regime execution remain deferred.

core_rule.statement: Recursive continuation semantics apply only after EVAL_024 and only to explicit recursive references that satisfy GuardRec(C); bounded unfolding may proceed through Unfold(Rec(C)) while preserving process equivalence where defined; lawful recursion that exceeds the current calculus boundary returns pNF(C), and recursive guard failure returns classified ⊥C_x; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Introduce recursive continuation structure as the first expressiveness extension after bounded strategy correctness, while preserving the existing reduction kernel and keeping recovery, sigma_RT, and operational-regime execution deferred.

canonical_claims.statement: Recursive continuation structure is explicit only; implicit self-reference is inadmissible.
Recursive unfolding is gated by GuardRec(C) and the bounded recursive depth boundary.
Lawful recursive continuation that exceeds the current calculus boundary returns pNF(C).
Recursive admissibility failure returns classified continuation failure ⊥C_x.

formal_objects.title: Recursive Continuation
formal_objects.canonical_form: Rec(C) := explicit recursive continuation expression with guarded self-reference
formal_objects.formal_definition: A continuation expression whose lawful evaluation may refer back to a prior continuation state under an explicit recursive admissibility guard.

formal_objects.title: Recursive Unfolding
formal_objects.canonical_form: Unfold(Rec(C)) := bounded expansion of an admissible recursive continuation into a continuation sequence
formal_objects.formal_definition: The bounded expansion of a recursive continuation into an admissible continuation sequence.

formal_objects.title: Recursive Admissibility Guard
formal_objects.canonical_form: GuardRec(C) := recursive admissibility condition governing lawful unfolding
formal_objects.formal_definition: The condition that determines whether a recursive continuation may lawfully unfold.

formal_objects.title: Recursive Depth Boundary
formal_objects.canonical_form: depthRec(C) := bounded recursive depth available under the current calculus boundary
formal_objects.formal_definition: The bounded recursive depth available to a recursive continuation under the current calculus boundary.

formal_objects.title: Recursive Continuation Class
formal_objects.canonical_form: ClassRec := {C | Rec(C) is explicit, guarded, and bounded or deferred as pNF(C)}
formal_objects.formal_definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to recursive admissibility and bounded unfolding behavior.

requirements: depthRec(C) bounded or classified as pNF(C)
Unfolding preserves process equivalence where defined

recursive_pipeline.operation: Detect explicit recursive continuation structure Rec(C).
If admissible and bounded, apply Unfold(Rec(C)).
If recursion is lawful but not presently unfoldable, return pNF(C).
If recursive admissibility fails, return classified ⊥C_x.

recursive_classes.description: Recursive continuation admits lawful bounded unfolding.
Recursive continuation is lawful but exceeds the current calculus boundary and returns pNF(C).
Recursive continuation violates admissibility and returns classified ⊥C_x.

admissibility_rules: Recursive depth must be bounded or deferred as pNF(C).
Recursive unfolding must preserve typed continuation rules.
Recursive unfolding must preserve process equivalence where defined.

relationships.reduction: REDUCE_025 may reduce recursive continuations only after recursive admissibility is established.
relationships.partial_normal_form: Lawful but currently unexpandable recursion terminates as pNF(C).
relationships.failure: Recursive guard failure returns a classified continuation failure.
relationships.termination: Recursive termination is not universally asserted by this patch.
relationships.strategy: S(C) may select recursive unfolding only as an admissible candidate.

invariants: Recursive continuation does not introduce recovery.
Recursive continuation does not introduce sigma_RT.
Recursive continuation does not execute operational regimes.
Recursive unfolding is bounded or deferred.
